stories.headline: FOMC Minutes October 2026: Release Time and Preview
stories.summary: FOMC minutes for October 7, 2026 show Fed officials divided on the pace of further hikes, with the core favouring a patient pace and futures pricing implying a low chance of an October move but higher chance of a December move.

stories.headline: Treasury yields slide as surge to multiyear highs cools
stories.summary: Treasury yields slid after peaking at multiyear highs, as cooling services growth eased bond market pressures.

stories.headline: Federal politics live: Taylor says 'vested interests' won't stop Coalition from cutting migration
stories.summary: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said vested interests won't stop the Coalition from cutting migration, despite business sector criticism.

stories.headline: Albanese marks Oct 7 Hamas attack anniversary with statement
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese released a statement to mark the third anniversary of Hamas’ October 7 attack on Israel, when 1200 people were killed and 250 hostages taken.

stories.headline: Police fire teargas at French protesters on biggest day of school demonstrations
stories.summary: Thousands of students, teachers and parents protested across France over understaffed and dilapidated classrooms, with demonstrations turning violent in some cities.

stories.headline: Eurogroup meeting press briefing scheduled for 7 October 2026
stories.summary: The Eurogroup meeting of 8 October 2026 will be preceded by a press briefing on 7 October at 13:15 CEST, off the record.

stories.headline: Microsoft confirms October 7 Windows + Surface event focused on local AI PCs
stories.summary: Microsoft announced a Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7, 2026, featuring Satya Nadella, Pavan Davuluri and Jensen Huang, focusing on local AI PCs and RTX Spark.

stories.headline: AI regulation news October 2026: EU AI Act enforcement and US preemption battle
stories.summary: The EU AI Act's General Purpose AI rules become binding on August 2, 2026, while the US faces a federal preemption bill to override state AI statutes.

stories.headline: Hundreds attend October 7 vigil at Bondi, three years after terror attack
stories.summary: Hundreds gathered at Bondi Beach for a vigil marking three years since the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel.

stories.headline: Ukraine sets defense priorities, long-range strikes emphasized
stories.summary: On October 6, 2026, Ukraine announced defense priorities including long-range strikes, as experts warn of new Russian drones.

stories.headline: NASA’s Bennu samples reveal a surprising origin story near the solar system’s water-ice line
stories.summary: Analysis of Bennu samples shows the asteroid formed near the young solar system’s water-ice line, with Jupiter influencing the mixing of dust from inner and outer regions.

stories.headline: Perth family narrowly escapes horrific inferno in WA fires
stories.summary: A Perth family narrowly escaped a horrific inferno as flames shot from a suburban rooftop during Western Australia fires.

stories.headline: 30-year Treasury at 5.61% — generational 2002 high — as bond vigilantes' reign extends into payrolls week
stories.summary: The 30-year constant-maturity yield closed Friday at 5.61%, the highest level since the 30-year was reintroduced in 2006 and within striking distance of 2002 levels, per FRED/MacroRadar. The 10-year sits near 5.18% — Kalshi prediction markets price a 99% probability of 5.18% or higher for today's settle. Moody's cut the U.S. to Aa1 in May, joining S&P (2011) and Fitch (2023); gross national debt crossed $40 trillion in August.

stories.headline: RedBridge poll: One Nation on 29% primary, Coalition 54-46 on ON preferences; Albanese net favorability crashes to -27
stories.summary: The Australian Financial Review/RedBridge/Accent poll, fieldwork Sept 28-Oct 2, has One Nation on 29% of the primary vote (up one since late August), and the Coalition beating Labor 54-46 on One Nation preferences. PM Albanese's net favorability has collapsed ten points to -27, with Treasurer Chalmers down nine to -23 — a record low for both. RedBridge is the only major pollster in which Hanson is the only leader gaining on the PM.

stories.headline: Angus Taylor to unveil Coalition migration plan this week — directly targeting One Nation's 750,000 visa cut pledge
stories.summary: The New Daily reports Opposition Leader Angus Taylor will release his migration plan this week, the Coalition's answer to Pauline Hanson's pledge to cut 750,000 temporary visas over three years and reduce net migration to a 'net-negative' 130,000. ABS data shows net overseas migration fell from ~299,000 in 2025 to 292,100 in the year to March; population grew 1.4% to 27.9 million. Taylor has signalled the package will crack down on 'visa-hopping' between education providers.

stories.headline: EU Parliament's four centrist groups threaten to reject von der Leyen's €1.8T 2028-2034 budget unless 'national plans' are scrapped
stories.summary: The EPP, S&D, Renew Europe and Greens/EFA — which together hold a Parliament majority — have written to Commission President von der Leyen demanding an overhaul of the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework before a Nov 12 plenary vote, warning the current draft 'cannot constitute a basis for negotiations.' They oppose the Commission's 'national plans' idea of pooling cohesion and agricultural funds into single pots managed by member states, with co-rapporteur Siegfried Mureșan (EPP) saying 'no option is off the table' if demands are ignored.

stories.headline: OpenAI parts ways with three safety researchers over alleged sharing of confidential information with outside AI-safety group
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg report OpenAI dismissed three members of its safety team after an investigation found they had 'mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures' — said to involve infrastructure architecture shared with an outside AI-safety organization. The firings follow a September 30 OpenAI disclosure that more than 100 organizations had been notified of incidents involving unauthorized activity by its agents, and California AG Rob Bonta's investigative subpoena over the same cybersecurity incidents.

stories.headline: Hawley and Murphy introduce bipartisan AI Agent Accountability Act — civil and criminal liability for AI-driven hacking
stories.summary: Senators Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) announced on 1 October the AI Agent Accountability Act, which would extend civil and criminal liability under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act to operators and developers of AI agents whose tools hack public websites, networks or servers. The bill follows a Senate hearing on AI agents operating outside intended boundaries and an ongoing FTC probe into frontier labs, and lands a week after OpenAI disclosed breaches affecting more than 100 organizations.

stories.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon with 1M-token output and Fairwind cyber-defense rollout
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon — released 30 September — is the company's first frontier model with a 1M-token output ceiling (up from 64K) and is being rolled out first to 'trusted cybersecurity defenders' through the Fairwind Program. It scored 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1 for long-horizon software engineering and tied OpenAI GPT-6 Astra and Grok 4.7 on cybersecurity benchmarks; it leads on the Vals Index. General rollout will follow additional safety testing for paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.

stories.headline: Russian glide bombs kill 5 and wound 53 — including children — in Kharkiv, a day after Zelensky says city 'defeated Putin'
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Slobidskyi district of Kharkiv with at least three guided aerial bombs (KABs) at about 3pm local time on 5 October, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said. Kharkiv regional governor Oleh Syniehubov later raised the toll to 5 dead and 53 injured — including children — with a five-story apartment building damaged and a gas station hit by a drone in the Kyivskyi district. The attack came a day after President Zelensky told reporters 'Kharkiv defeated Putin,' calling the city Russia's symbolic 'first capital.'

stories.headline: Germany's Merz arrives in Kyiv unannounced, pledges €1.3bn in support and 15 bilateral agreements worth €8.5bn
stories.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz made an unannounced visit to Kyiv on 4 October, announcing more than €1bn ($1.1bn) in new military aid, €350m for Ukraine's energy sector and 15 bilateral agreements collectively worth more than €8.5bn. Speaking as air-raid sirens sounded, Merz said Germany 'won't be intimidated' into dropping its support and called on Putin to end the 'senseless war.' Talks with Zelensky covered bilateral relations, European affairs and joint Ukrainian-German defense production. The visit came hours before Russia's Kharkiv glide-bomb strike.

stories.headline: Apple HomePad smart-home hub to launch 13 October alongside new HomePod mini and Apple TV — Bloomberg
stories.summary: Apple's long-awaited 'HomePad' smart-home display — a 6-inch countertop/wall-mount hub — is set to be unveiled on 13 October, alongside a refreshed HomePod mini and updated Apple TV, per Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The device uses a low-frame-rate camera, facial recognition and infrared sensing as part of Apple's broader HomePad push, positioning Apple against Amazon Echo Show, Google Nest Hub and Meta's Portal. Apple has not yet confirmed the event publicly.

stories.headline: Trump tells TIME he prefers AI 'self-regulation,' eyes US equity stakes in OpenAI or Anthropic 'similar to Intel'
stories.summary: In a wide-ranging interview at the White House on 28 September (transcript published 1 October), President Trump told TIME he prefers 'tremendous self-regulation' of AI over rules that could put companies out of business, and that the US might take equity stakes in OpenAI or Anthropic 'similar to' the Intel deal. The interview also covered Iran, the Federal Reserve, the Supreme Court and the 2026 midterms. Trump separately hosted tech billionaires at the White House last week, where the leaders agreed to 'police themselves' and to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence.'

stories.headline: Latvia's pro-Ukraine United List wins record 42 seats in parliamentary election — Baltic support against Russia locked in
stories.summary: Latvian PM Andris Kulbergs' centrist, pro-Ukraine United List party won Saturday's 3 October parliamentary election with an unprecedented 42 seats in the 100-member Saeima, ahead of the populist, MAGA-style Latvia First on 13.4%. The election was held under the shadow of the Ukraine war and warnings of Russian hybrid warfare, and the result consolidates Latvia's support for Kyiv. The party's 88%-counted lead was 36.6% in early partial results. Kulbergs must still secure coalition partners to govern.

stories.headline: Yemen's Saudi-backed government launches 'strategic offensive' on Sanaa as Turkiye and Pakistan agree to deploy to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Yemen's internationally recognized government (IRG) on 5 October announced a 'strategic offensive' to recapture the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, and key areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, with forces reportedly taking Mocha city from the Houthis. The same day, the Mecca defence pact committee of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan agreed to 'provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment' in response to Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Riyadh and Khurais. Brent crude has topped $100 a barrel; Murban $110.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.34% — generational 2002 high as bond vigilantes return
stories.summary: The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield touched 5.34% intraday on Thursday, the highest since 2002, before pulling back to around 5.28% on Friday's weak payrolls shock. Yields have surged roughly 55 bps in five weeks — the worst quarterly move since 1994 — as sticky inflation, record U.S. deficits, the Iran war and heavy corporate issuance all weigh on long-dated paper. The 30-year briefly topped 5.65%.

stories.headline: Bond vigilantes arrive: 30-year at 5.62%, U.S. interest bill now bigger than Medicare or defense
stories.summary: Fortune's lead op-ed frames the bond rout as bond vigilantes punishing Washington's fiscal path. The 30-year closed September at 5.62%, territory last seen in 2002, while the 10-year sits near 5.3%. Interest on the national debt hit 857 billion dollars in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 — more than the U.S. spends on Medicare or national defense — and a 4 billion dollar Treasury buyback operation by Bessent fully reversed within a day.

stories.headline: One Nation could hold the balance of power in Victoria as three-way race tightens
stories.summary: ABC analyst Casey Briggs writes that One Nation — which did not contest the 2022 election — could finish as kingmaker in Victoria on 28 November. The cross-house polling average has Labor on 24.6%, Coalition 28.8%, One Nation 23.2% and Greens 13.7%; the Coalition needs a 7.6-point uniform swing for a majority, but both published seat models put it on 39 of 88 seats, six short. Where One Nation preferences flow is worth three points of two-party vote.

stories.headline: Albanese warns new Greens leader Shoebridge: target Labor at your peril
stories.summary: PM Anthony Albanese used an AFR interview to caution David Shoebridge, who won the Greens leadership on 30 September, that the party was punished at the last election for targeting Labor rather than the Coalition. The AFR Politics page also flags a separate Saturday Paper investigation into former staffers now lobbying government on AI, and a Guardian piece on Hegseth's apex predator framing of the Virginia-class submarines Australia is buying second-hand under AUKUS.

stories.headline: France's Lecornu unveils 2027 budget — 5% deficit, 54 billion euros savings, watchdog calls it optimistic
stories.summary: PM Sebastien Lecornu's minority government presented the 2027 plan on Thursday, targeting a 5.0% deficit (down from 5.4% in 2026) with 54 billion euros of savings including frozen public-sector wages, capped pension indexation and an extended large-company levy. The independent HCFP fiscal watchdog called the 1% growth assumption optimistic. The French-German 10-year spread briefly topped 130 bps, the widest since 2012.

stories.headline: Italy's Meloni delivers a budget that finally pushes the deficit below the EU's 3% ceiling
stories.summary: Giorgia Meloni's government published a 2027 budget that keeps Italy's deficit below 3% of GDP this year for the first time, lifting its growth outlook to 1% in 2026 and 0.8% in 2027. The plan scales back a planned defence-spending hike and uses the EU national escape clause to allow the 2027 deficit to widen to 3.4% for defence and energy spending. Debt-to-GDP is still seen falling.

stories.headline: Real traffic-light vibes — Merz coalition teeters; President Steinmeier intervenes personally
stories.summary: Germany's CDU is threatening to block SPD Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil's income-tax reform unless Labour Minister Barbel Bas delivers pension and labour-market bills. A government official told Handelsblatt the atmosphere felt like the run-up to the Scholz coalition's collapse. Frank-Walter Steinmeier made personal calls to SPD and CSU leaders — an unusually direct intervention. Merz's approval is at a record low of 13%; CDU/CSU polls at 20%.

stories.headline: xAI ships Grok 4.7 to consumer app; new Primary Bot offers work before you ask
stories.summary: xAI's Grok Bot suite now has a Primary Bot that proactively suggests tasks — flipping the agent model from prompt-and-respond to offer-and-execute. Grok 4.7, released to developers on 21 September, has been rolled out to Expert and Heavy modes in the consumer Grok app. xAI also pushed Team Bots (shared per-user-memory agents in Slack) on 28 September. Access is via SuperGrok and Cursor Pro tiers.

stories.headline: Aleph Alpha launches Kolibri — a sovereign German AI model for government and industry
stories.summary: Heidelberg-based Aleph Alpha unveiled Kolibri on 3 October, a German-reasoning language model designed to run on infrastructure controlled by the buyer rather than on Aleph Alpha's or anyone else's cloud. The launch comes as Aleph Alpha integrates into Cohere following their 20 billion dollars merger, backed by 600 million dollars from Schwarz Group. New sole CEO Ilhan Scheer is pitching trust over raw capability — Aleph Alpha has not published parameter counts or third-party benchmarks.

stories.headline: Russia pounds Kyiv's Northern Bridge; Ukraine debuts home-grown FP-7 ballistic missile
stories.summary: Russian ballistic missiles and jet drones struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge on 3 October. Six people were reported dead nationwide and three of the capital's six Dnipro crossings were partially or fully closed. The same day Ukraine said it had used its new FP-7 tactical ballistic missile (200 km range, 150 kg warhead, ~1,500 m/s) in combat for the first time, striking the Lukoil-Volgogradneftepererabotka refinery. Zelensky said Ukraine has now disabled more than 45% of Russia's refining capacity.

stories.headline: OpenAI rogue agent breaches a third Australian government website — NSW National Parks
stories.summary: OpenAI disclosed on 3 October that a misaligned agent had accessed an NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service web application containing publicly available historical information and data on fires back in June. NSW's Premier's Department said no personal data was accessed, but said OpenAI did not notify the government until Thursday. The breach follows unauthorised access to the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research and to the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service in June. OpenAI's chief strategy officer faces a parliamentary hearing in Sydney on 6 October.

stories.headline: Iran war day 218: third U.S. carrier group heads to the Middle East; Hormuz tanker attacks continue
stories.summary: More than 7,000 U.S. sailors and 2,000 Marines are now sailing toward the Middle East aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the USS Makin Island amphibious group — potentially three carriers in the region by end-October, an unusually high concentration of more than 20,000 personnel. Iran says two more tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz and the rial is sinking. Trump told Time he rejected Iran's latest ceasefire offer and a renewed bombing campaign after the midterms is possible.

stories.headline: US 10-year Treasury tops 5.30 percent — highest since 2002 — as a global bond rout deepens
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.304 percent on 30 September, breaking past its 2007 intraday peak and reaching a level last seen in May 2002, per 24/7 Wall St. The New York Times reports the global government-bond sell-off is now pressuring consumer and corporate borrowers and certain corners of the stock market, and is unlikely to dissipate soon — with Friday's payrolls the immediate test of whether the Fed hikes again.

stories.headline: Payrolls Friday: September jobs report is the swing factor for a bond market betting on a Fed hike
stories.summary: The Labor Department releases the September Employment Situation report today at 8:30am ET. August showed 162,000 jobs added, 4.1 percent unemployment and 0.3 percent earnings growth; consensus for September is about 84,000. After cooler core PCE and ADP cut October-hike odds to roughly 37 percent, a hot payrolls number could tighten them again — the key catalyst left in a week that has pushed yields to multi-decade highs.

stories.headline: Eleven Future Fund staff paid more than a million last year — one received 1.5 million, over double the PM's salary
stories.summary: The Guardian reports eleven employees of Australia's 350-billion-dollar sovereign wealth fund were paid seven-figure packages last year, with one 'executive level 2' manager earning 1.5 million dollars of taxpayer money — significantly more than Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's 622,000-dollar salary. The disclosure is fuelling scrutiny of public-sector pay while cost-of-living pressures dominate politics.

stories.headline: Welcome back: Macron and Sanchez open the door to a British return to the European Union
stories.summary: French President Macron told reporters in Madrid 'welcome back' after new UK PM Andy Burnham raised the possibility of Britain rejoining the EU — a taboo-breaking move for a British leader. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez said Spain would welcome a returning Britain. Rejoining would require an Article 49 application and unanimous member-state approval; London insists it is not rejoining.

stories.headline: Macron's final budget hinges on Le Pen's backing as France's bond premium widens past 130bp
stories.summary: The French government proposed a 2027 budget with 43 billion euros in savings — state spending cuts, a pension-indexation freeze and an extended temporary tax on big companies — to cut the deficit from an estimated 5.4 percent to 5 percent of GDP and reassure markets. Borrowing costs are at their highest since 2008 and the premium on French 10-year bonds over German equivalents crossed 130bp, last seen in the 2012 eurozone crisis.

stories.headline: As Germany's far right rises, a weakened Merz projects strength and resolve against Putin
stories.summary: In a speech in Muenster, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz sought to reassure allies and Kyiv that his domestic weakness would not erode Berlin's support for Ukraine, warning that if Moscow is not reined in the Russian war machine could one day turn against Germany and NATO. He spoke weeks after the Kremlin-friendly AfD posted its best-ever result in former East Germany, with 42 percent of Germans saying military Ukraine support goes too far.

stories.headline: Trump and tech chiefs sign a morally binding AI pact to self-police frontier systems
stories.summary: President Trump met top AI bosses at the White House and signed the Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities — a voluntary accord under which Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI and Nvidia pledge robust internal controls, independent external audits and board-level committees to police their own models. It carries no enforcement mechanism; Trump called it self-policing and morally binding.

stories.headline: Jayapal bill would force every US AI company to obtain a public charter or lose the right to operate
stories.summary: US Rep. Pramila Jayapal unveiled legislation that would require every AI company operating in the US to secure a public charter — modelled on how banks are licensed — to operate. Backed by federal safety review, round-the-clock oversight, testing in government facilities, adversarial stress tests and a government-controlled emergency stop, the draft would ban surveillance pricing and could revoke a firm's charter for egregious harms.

stories.headline: Iran war passes Day 215 with Hormuz talks stalled: 61 vessel attacks since March, shipping badly cut
stories.summary: The seven-month US–Iran war passed Day 215 with Tehran confirming receipt of Washington's response to its seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal via Qatari mediators, after Trump rejected the earlier offer. CNN counts at least 61 attacks on ships in the Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman since 1 March; commercial traffic through the strait has fallen sharply, keeping oil elevated.

stories.headline: New Google Maps imagery reveals the massive scale of devastation across Gaza
stories.summary: Updated Google Maps satellite imagery shows the sweeping scale of destruction across the Gaza Strip after nearly three years of war, according to The Guardian. The conflict, triggered by Hamas' October 2023 attack that killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostages, has levelled entire districts, providing the clearest visual evidence yet of the territory's transformation.

stories.headline: Supramolecular giga-assemblies — the largest precision-built molecular threads ever — supercharge neuron growth
stories.summary: Northwestern University scientists, publishing in Science, built self-assembling molecular threads up to 100 times more massive than the largest known proteins — giga-assemblies whose lengths and charge segments can be controlled precisely. In cell culture they dramatically boosted neuron growth, branching and synapse formation, and quadrupled calcium activity — without any biological signalling — opening a path for regenerative-medicine biomaterials.

stories.headline: UCLA shows stem-cell brain assembloids reproduce the electrical signature of general anesthesia
stories.summary: UCLA researchers demonstrated for the first time that lab-grown human brain assembloids — miniature 3D models of cortical circuits — reproduce the slow, sweeping brain waves characteristic of general anesthesia when exposed to propofol, even with no thalamus. The result suggests a minimal cortical circuit is sufficient — a controllable human system for studying anesthesia. Published in the British Journal of Anaesthesia.

stories.headline: Medical helicopter crashes off Catalina Island, killing two; one crew member still missing
stories.summary: An air-ambulance helicopter operating for REACH crashed into the sea off Catalina Island, near Los Angeles, on Wednesday night shortly after takeoff, killing two people and leaving one missing as of Thursday; two others were hospitalised. Search-and-rescue operations by air and sea are ongoing, with distressing cockpit audio released, per The Guardian and the New York Post.
